grammar.title: Present Perfect for Experience (ever, never)
grammar.explanation:
We use the **present perfect** to talk about experiences in our life, when we don't say exactly when it happened. Form: **have** / **has** + past participle.

Use **ever** in questions about your whole life: ***Have** you **ever** waited at the **gate**?*

Use **never** with a positive verb to say it did not happen in your life: *I**'ve never** missed a train.*

When you say **when** it happened, use the past simple: *I **went** there in 2022.* A common mistake is *Have you ever went?* — always use the past participle: **been**, **seen**, **eaten**.
examples: *I**'ve been** to Canada twice. (experience + how many times)
***Have** you **ever eaten** octopus? (ever in a question)
*She**'s never driven** a car. (never + past participle)

practice.q: Ask about life experience: you / ever / wait at the gate
practice.a: Have you ever waited at the gate?

practice.q: Make it negative with never: I / carry / a heavy bag
practice.a: I have never carried a heavy bag. / I've never carried a heavy bag.

practice.q: Make a question with ever: she / arrive / late at the airport
practice.a: Has she ever arrived late at the airport?

practice.q: Fix the mistake: Have you ever went to the corner?
practice.a: Have you ever been to the corner?
